title: ZEN: Empowering Distributed Training with Sparsity-driven Data Synchronization
problem: Distributed training systems face significant communication bottlenecks when synchronizing gradients across multiple nodes, with bandwidth and latency limitations preventing efficient scaling. Traditional approaches transmit complete gradient updates, wasting communication bandwidth on non-critical values.
motivation: Communication overhead is a critical bottleneck in distributed training that directly limits scalability and efficiency of large-scale model training across clusters.
method: ZEN identifies sparse patterns in gradient updates and uses this sparsity to drive a selective synchronization protocol. The system transmits only sparse, high-impact gradients to reduce communication volume, adapts the synchronization strategy based on observed sparsity, and maintains convergence properties while reducing overall data transfer requirements.
key_novelty: Using gradient sparsity patterns to intelligently optimize the data synchronization protocol in distributed training, reducing communication overhead without sacrificing convergence.
contributions: Sparsity-aware synchronization mechanism that reduces gradient communication volume
Adaptive protocol that exploits temporal and spatial sparsity patterns
System implementation demonstrating improved training efficiency and scalability
Empirical evaluation showing speedup gains with reduced communication costs

metrics.speedup: training time improvement through communication reduction
metrics.other: communication volume reduction, network bandwidth utilization

limitations: Not discussed (analyzed from title only, no abstract provided)
